title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 26 (Agreement in restraint of marriage, void)

content.overview: Section 26 provides that every agreement in restraint of the marriage of any person, other than a minor, is void.
content.glance: Agreement in restraint of marriage of any person other than a minor is void.
content.study: Every agreement in restraint of the marriage of any person, other than a minor, is void. The exception for a minor is built into the section. Current-law framing: identify the restraint of marriage; confirm the person is not a minor; conclude voidness under s. 26.

sections.heading: Restraint of marriage
sections.body: Every agreement in restraint of the marriage of any person, other than a minor, is void.

provisions.title: Agreement in restraint of marriage, void

examples.title: Adult restraint
examples.body: A agrees not to marry B (an adult) in return for payment. The agreement is void under s. 26.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 26 apply to a minor?
hypotheticals.analysis: The section voids restraint of marriage of any person other than a minor — so the restraint-of-marriage voidness rule is stated for non-minors.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-26
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: Only total lifelong bans on marriage are void.
misconceptions.correction: Section 26 voids every agreement in restraint of the marriage of any person other than a minor.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 26 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify restraint of marriage. II. Confirm person is not a minor. III. Conclude void under s. 26.

examTips: State the minor exception in the section itself.
